November 13, 20265:01 AM ET
By

STANWOOD, WASHINGTON - DECEMBER 6: In an aerial view, floodwaters surround a home on December 6, 2023 in Stanwood, Washington. Atmospheric river conditions in the region brought heavy rains and flooding.
David Ryder/Getty Images

It's the wettest time of the year for one of the wettest parts of the country: the Pacific Northwest.
This week is no exception as heavy rain, high tides and a rising sea level hit the West Coast.
And more storms are on their way.
Two atmospheric rivers, bringing heavy rain, will pound parts of Oregon and Washington state back-to-back on Friday and Saturday. Two other atmospheric rivers already dropped multiple inches of rain on both states earlier this week.

Democratic victories in the South this year were driven just as much by who showed up to vote as who stayed home, according to an NPR analysis of turnout data.

Midterm elections normally have lower voter participation than presidential contests. But from Louisiana to the Carolinas, counties that voted for former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 came closer to matching — and in some cases exceeding — presidential turnout. At the same time, counties won by President Trump saw a much sharper decline in turnout and fewer Republican votes.

item.description:

By
Noam Levey
YouTube

HILLSBORO, N.D. — The Kritzberger family has farmed in the Red River Valley for more than a century. They once had livestock. Now they grow sugar beets, soybeans and grains.
Like many farmers, they labor to balance the books.
Health Reporting in the States

"We're in an incredible amount of debt," Ang Kritzberger said as she walked the farm on a recent fall morning.
For the past 10 years, the Kritzbergers have had another worry. Their daughter Nina has Type 1 diabetes. That landed the family in a national debate about how to protect patients from high insulin costs.
Nina was diagnosed when she was 7.
"I slept by her bedside for the first 60 days," Ang Kritzberger said. "And I had to stick her finger every two hours, 24 hours a day, to make sure that she was OK."

item.title: Why even a fraction of a degree can escalate climate change impacts
item.description:
Climate
Why even a fraction of a degree can escalate climate change impacts
November 13, 20265:00 AM ET
Lauren Sommer
Coral reefs are highly vulnerable to heat, like these bleached corals in Thailand in 2024. If the planet continues to warm at the current rate, the majority of the world's reefs aren't likely to survive.
Sirachai Arunrugstichai/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Sirachai Arunrugstichai/Getty Images
Countries have gathered at the annual climate change negotiations at the COP31 summit in Turkey to discuss how to achieve a goal that is increasingly unachievable. A decade ago, countries agreed to limit climate warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit). Now, that goal is out of reach.
Globally, average temperatures are already close to 1.5 degrees Celsius warmer than they were before the Industrial Revolution. Heat-trapping emissions from burning fossil fuels are still rising in the atmosphere, and most countries are not on track to meet their climate pledges to cut emissions by transitioning to cleaner energy.

item.description:

The cost of college is confusing. Some schools are trying to change that

By
Jon Marcus
,
Liam Elder-Connors
An aerial view of the Middlebury College campus in Vermont. Middlebury is among a number of colleges trying to help people decipher how much they actually cost, by guaranteeing free tuition for families with incomes under a particular threshold.
Oliver Parini for The Hechinger Report
hide caption
toggle caption i
Oliver Parini for The Hechinger Report
Catch up on what you missed with our Education newsletter, sent weekly.
MIDDLEBURY, Vt. — Stately buildings of Vermont limestone surround meticulously tended lawns in a village that could be the setting for a Hallmark Christmas movie.
Middlebury College looks … expensive. But like other universities and colleges, it's working hard to persuade people that it's not.
Middlebury has announced that students from families with household incomes up to $175,000 can enroll tuition-free. That makes it one of a growing number of colleges trying to reduce widespread public confusion about what college actually costs.

item.title: Rosalía and Milo J take top awards as Daddy Yankee is paid tribute at Latin Grammys
item.description:
Music
Rosalía and Milo J take top awards as Daddy Yankee is paid tribute at Latin Grammys
November 13, 20264:57 AM ET
Felix Contreras
Yahritza y Su Esencia and Rosalía accept Song Of The Year for "La Perla" onstage during the 27th Annual Latin GRAMMY Awards at MGM Grand Garden Arena on November 12, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Kevin Winter/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Kevin Winter/Getty Images
The 27th annual Latin Grammy's wrapped up in Las Vegas last night with a big night for Argentine folk music, a very big surprise award presenter and a newly minted U.S. congressman taking home a Latin Grammy statuette.
In an industry in which either reggaeton beats or polished pop productions dominate the charts and sales, folk music-powered 20-year-old Argentine vocalist Milo J took home the award for Record of the Year for his single Niño, as well as Best Folk Album for La Vida Era Más Corta, Best Urban/Urban Fusion performance, and Best Recording Package.
Spanish vocalist Rosalía swept several top categories including Album of the Year and Best Alternative Album for LUX, Song of the Year, Best Pop Song and Best Short Form Music Video.
